results.title: The reference, measured in THIS window: declared 1px, and `thin` beside it

checks.label: --oc-border-hairline resolves to a non-empty value on :root
the two synthetic elements were alive in the document together when read
THE SESSION'S PREMISE, measured in this window: `thin` and a declared `1px` have the SAME used width
var(--oc-border-hairline) and a declared `1px` have the SAME used width
the reference is ORDERED thin < medium < thick, so the probe distinguishes the keywords

notes: MEASURED FRESH IN THIS WINDOW: border-width:thin -> 0.8px; border-width:1px -> 0.8px; border-width:var(--oc-border-hairline) -> 0.8px; medium -> 2.4px; thick -> 4.8px; devicePixelRatio=1.0000000149011612
declared-to-computed ladder in this window: 1px->0.8px 2px->1.6px 3px->2.4px 4px->4px 5px->4.8px — these are declared INPUTS whose computed values are read, not expectations.

A declared 1px does NOT compute to the string "1px" here: it computes 0.8px. That is this display's device-pixel quantization, not a token failure — and it is why every border check below is an EQUALITY against this measured reference rather than against any literal.
